entries.mechanism:
The pinned TAXSIM 2.30.0 binary's 2026 law year does not model the
qualifying-child credit machinery (documented in docs/policyengine-
taxsim.md and verified against the binary: 2025 models the full OBBBA
$2,200/child credit, 2026 returns only the $500 other-dependent path).
On every selected row TAXSIM's v22 equals exactly 500 x depx (or zero),
while the axiom side computes the enacted 26 USC 24 credit. NBER model
gap, not an Axiom defect.

Same 2026 TAXSIM gap as the CTC class: EITC with qualifying children
returns zero at the 2026 law year (childless EITC is modeled; 2025
models both). Every selected row has depx > 0, TAXSIM v25 = 0, and a
positive axiom EITC under the enacted 26 USC 32. NBER model gap, not an
Axiom defect.

Every residual is an exact whole multiple of the 2026 section 63(f)
additional standard deduction ($2,050 unmarried / $1,650 per married
individual). The TAXSIM input format carries no blindness column and its
aged handling differs from the ECPS leaves the axiom projection reads
(is_blind and per-member age), so axiom counts more 63(f) increments
than TAXSIM can see. Input-format scope difference, not a computation
disagreement.

On every selected wages-only row the summed axiom statute targets
(us:statutes/26/3101/a plus 3101/b/1) equal exactly 7.65 per cent of
total tax-unit wages, including units with wages far above the 2026
contribution and benefit base — the encoded rules apply no 26 USC
3121(a)(1) cap, while TAXSIM (and PolicyEngine) cap the OASDI portion
per employee. Tracked upstream in axiom-encode#1214.

All remaining employee_fica residual rows involve the SECA (26 USC
1401/1402) chain; signs are mixed and no single-rate signature fits, so
the class is fingerprinted for pull-one-case triage (axiom-oracles#304
lists the representative case) rather than asserted. Classified on the
axiom side because the uncapped-OASDI gap (axiom-encode#1214) already
contaminates every SECA-adjacent sum.

Each selected liability residual reproduces, within $15, the sum of the
unit's own component-class residuals (CTC and EITC 2026 TAXSIM gaps, AMT
and tax-before-credits classes) minus TAXSIM's niit and addmed outputs —
NIIT because the composed axiom program excludes us:statutes/26/1411
until the upstream duplicate-rule encoding is fixed (axiom-encode#1213),
additional Medicare because TAXSIM folds it into fiitax while the axiom
liability target excludes it. No independent liability-level
disagreement remains on these rows.

TAXSIM's input schema has no blindness column, so the 63(f) additional
standard deduction axiom applies from ECPS-observed blind facts ($2,050
single / $1,650 married per blind filer or spouse, 2026) has no TAXSIM
counterpart. Extension of the original class to newly verified rows:
each selected row's difference equals the case's blind member count
times the filing-status increment, verified against the loaded ECPS
blind facts; taxable/tax/liability rows are the same delta propagated
(chain rows selected only when blindness is the case's sole leaf
divergence and the downstream delta is bounded by the top marginal rate
on the increment).

For filers whose income is dominated by capital gains and dividends,
axiom's tax computation routes through the capital-gains worksheet
concepts while the mapped tax_before_credits bucket carries zero, and
TAXSIM reports the schedule total in its tbc column — yet final
liability agrees within 2 percent on every selected row. A concept-
bucket routing artifact of the comparison mapping, not a tax
disagreement; the liability agreement is the proof.

The comparison bridge follows the PolicyEngine convention that rental
income is qualified business income for 26 USC 199A, while the TAXSIM
projection necessarily carries rental income in TAXSIM's otherprop
column, which TAXSIM defines as non-QBI property income. On every
selected row TAXSIM's idtl=2 decomposition shows taxable income equal
to AGI minus the (correct 2026) standard deduction with zero QBI
deduction, while axiom grants the bridge QBID on rental/SE income:
either the H.R.1 section 70105 minimum deduction of $400 (floor rows,
where the wage/UBIA phase-in has extinguished the regular deduction or
20% of QBI is below the floor) or 20% of QBI in the phase region. The
taxable-income difference equals the recomputed bridge QBID within
$0.05 on every selected row (verifier: QBI = otherprop + max(0,psemp)
+ max(0,ssemp) - SECA ALD; phaseout start 403500/201750, length
150000/75000; floor 400 gated on QBI >= 1000). A divergence of engine
conventions about the same household, not an axiom encoding error.

The same TAXSIM-side Colorado flat-tax offset already triangulated in
the co-state-income-tax-taxsim suite (axiom equals PolicyEngine on
every one of these tax units; the divergence is TAXSIM's Colorado
vintage, a TABOR-mechanism rate/threshold difference). Every case id
selected here is identically a member of the corresponding
triangulated class in dispositions/co-state-income-tax-taxsim.yaml;
the observed intersection-lane deltas sit within 5 cents of the same
flat values (30.80 MFJ, 20.70 single).

Triangulated TAXSIM-side divergence in Colorado's refundable credit
stack: on every selected row axiom and PolicyEngine agree on Colorado
liability to the cent (the tax unit is absent from the complete
31-row axiom-vs-PE mismatch set for the same 1,201-unit population),
while TAXSIM's own idtl=2 state decomposition shows the divergence
arising in its state credit columns (sctc family-affordability/CTC,
srebate) rather than the flat-tax leg: staxbc matches the rate
mechanics while net siitax departs, going negative on refundable-
credit households. TAXSIM's 2026-05-21 Colorado module carries a
different family-affordability-credit vintage (the credit's TABOR
scale factor is determined annually) and couples its Colorado EITC to
its broken 2026 federal credit machinery. These rows have no federal
taxable-income mismatch: the divergence is entirely state-side.

TAXSIM's 2026 federal EITC applies the CHILDLESS schedule to tax
units with qualifying children: on every selected row TAXSIM's value
sits exactly on the 2026 childless curve - phase-in at 7.65% of
earnings to the cent, the $664 childless maximum on plateau rows, and
phase-out rows solving to the statutory $10,860 childless phase-out
start on independent incomes - while axiom's value sits on the
with-children statutory curve (45% of $9,512 = $4,280.40 observed
4,280.31 three-child phase-in; 40% of $17,493 = $6,997.20 observed
6,997.18 two-child). The same missing-2026-credit-machinery root as
the dispositioned CTC class.

Refundable-arm face of the dispositioned TAXSIM 2026 child-credit
machinery gap: on every selected row axiom equals the statutory 2026
value exactly - either the full entitlement 2,200 per qualifying
child plus 500 per other dependent, or the additional-CTC cap of 15%
of earnings above 2,500 (e.g. 0.15 x (28,426 - 2,500) = 3,888.90 vs
observed 3,888.91) - while TAXSIM returns pre-TCJA-vintage machinery
output inconsistent with any 2026 schedule.

Concept-bucket routing artifact of the comparison mapping, re-verified
on the 2026-07-27 report generated under both dividend-qualification
fixes: on every selected row the mapped axiom tax_before_credits
bucket carries the ordinary-schedule component while the
preferential-rate capital-gains/qualified-dividend worksheet tax
rides in a different concept bucket, and TAXSIM's v28 tbc column
reports the worksheet total - yet FINAL LIABILITY AGREES within the
$15 comparison tolerance on every selected row (none of these cases
has a liability mismatch), with ctc, eitc, cdcc and amt all compared
and matched on the same cases. The agreement of the total while the
bucket split differs is the proof: not a tax disagreement.
Verified per-row via TAXSIM idtl=2 reruns (probe: axiom tbc 22,381.42
+ routed preferential component 5,449.08 = TAXSIM v28 27,830.50 =
fiitax exactly).

Concept-scope bridge artifact on the liability mapping: axiom's
federal liability bucket is 26 USC 6401 chapter-1 income tax, while
TAXSIM's fiitax additionally folds in the chapter-2A net investment
income tax and the chapter-2 additional Medicare tax. On every
selected row the liability difference equals exactly
-(TAXSIM niit + TAXSIM addmed) from the idtl=2 decomposition run on
the same input rows (remainder <= $0.60), i.e. the engines agree on
chapter-1 tax and differ only in which surtaxes the mapped bucket
carries.

Intersection-lane echo of the triangulated TAXSIM Colorado refundable-credit vintage divergence: on every selected row the intersection state-liability difference equals, to within five cents, the difference already dispositioned as taxsim-co-refundable-credit- vintage for the identical tax unit in the co-state-income-tax-taxsim suite (where axiom equals PolicyEngine on the same unit - none of these case ids appears in the 31-row axiom-vs-PE mismatch set for the same 1,201-unit population). Delta equality across the two lanes proves the intersection row carries the same TAXSIM-side state credit-stack divergence, not a new intersection artifact, even where the unit also has a dispositioned federal-side residual.

Liability face of the dispositioned TAXSIM 2026 credit-machinery gaps on zero-net-pre-credit-tax rows, verified per row against the pinned binary (cdate 2026-05-21) rerun with idtl=2 on the persisted input rows: TAXSIM v28 is fully absorbed by its v22 (500 x depx path) and fiitax equals -(v25 childless-schedule EITC), while axiom liability equals -(axiom EITC + min(1,700 x qualifying children, axiom refundable-capped CTC)). On all twelve rows L_liab - (-(L_eitc + ACTC)) = 0.00 exactly, i.e. the whole difference is the sum of the already-dispositioned EITC-schedule and CTC/ACTC machinery gaps; no independent liability-level disagreement.

Nonrefundable-arm liability face of the dispositioned TAXSIM 2026 child-credit machinery gap: the federal liability difference equals -(2,200 - 500) x 3 qualifying children exactly - axiom applies the enacted 26 USC 24 credit (3 x 2,200 nonrefundable, liability sufficient to absorb it) while TAXSIM v22 carries only the 500 x depx other-dependent path (v22 = 1,500 on the idtl=2 rerun of the pinned binary against the persisted input row). Same mechanism as taxsim-2026-ctc-child-credit-machinery-absent, surfacing at the liability bucket because the ctc bucket compares the refundable-capped value.

Chain propagation of the dispositioned QBID rental-convention taxable-income class (taxsim-qbid-rental-convention-taxable-income) into the tax-before-credits bucket: on every selected row the case's taxable_income row is claimed by that class and the tax-before-credits difference equals exactly one statutory 2026 bracket rate (10/12/22/24 per cent) times the taxable-income difference, within $0.60 - ordinary-bracket propagation of the same convention delta, no independent tax computation disagreement.

Blindness 63(f) class member whose axiom taxable income floors at zero: TAXSIM (no blindness column) computes taxable income 997.52 under the 16,100 single standard deduction, while axiom's 18,150 (16,100 + 2,050 blind increment, the case's dispositioned standard_deduction row) exceeds AGI, so axiom taxable income clamps to 0 and the difference equals -997.52, the truncated remainder of the same 63(f) increment rather than a whole multiple.

Compound of two dispositioned mechanisms on one row: the 63(f) blindness increment (2,050 single, the case's dispositioned standard_deduction row) plus the H.R.1 section 70105 QBID minimum deduction of 400 that the bridge grants on the case's 8,860 of rental (otherprop) income while TAXSIM applies no QBID to otherprop (the dispositioned QBID rental convention). The taxable-income difference equals -(2,050 + 400) within a cent.

AGI-side propagation of the fingerprinted SECA chain drift: every selected row's tax unit carries self-employment income and its employee_fica row is already classified under axiom-seca-chain-drift-pending-triage, so the half-SECA above-the- line deduction and the QBI base both inherit the same axiom-side drift and no clean single-mechanism arithmetic fits (135628 additionally compounds its dispositioned 1,650 blindness increment). Classified on the axiom side pending the same pull-one-case triage as the parent class; not counted as explained.

Bracket-rate propagation of the SECA-chain-contaminated taxable-income rows (axiom-seca-chain-drift-taxable-income- propagation) into tax before credits: on every selected row the tax-before-credits difference equals exactly one statutory 2026 bracket rate (10/12/22/24/37 per cent) times the case's taxable-income difference, within $0.60 - pure propagation, no independent divergence. Classified axiom-side with the parent SECA drift class; not counted as explained.

mstat=1 unit carries dependents (depx >= 1): the pinned 2.30.0
binary's v13 shows the $24,150 HoH standard deduction and the HoH
rate schedule flows through v18/v19/v28/fiitax. The oracle bridge
files these units single on both engines' inputs, and the axiom
side computes the single-filer statute it was given. Verified by
binary replay on 2026-08-23 over the affected units: rerunning the
exact persisted taxsim_input row reproduces the reported TAXSIM
value to the cent, with v13 = 24,150 the only divergence trigger
(axiom-oracles#439's first verified-but-unenrollable mechanism,
enrollable now that every mismatch row persists).

Standard-deduction face of the auto-itemize mechanism already
enrolled for this unit's liability and tax-before-credits rows:
TAXSIM itemizes (v17 = 18,352.57 > 16,100 on solo replay,
2026-08-24) and reports v13 = 0, while the axiom side reports the
section 63(c) standard deduction. Delta is exactly -16,100.

Downstream shadow of taxsim-qbid-rental-convention-taxable-income at the
unit's ordinary marginal rate. On every selected row (a) the taxable-income
row is dispositioned to that entry - axiom grants 26 USC 199A QBID on
rental/SE income (H.R.1 section 70105 $400 minimum deduction on the floor
rows, 20% of QBI in the phase region) while TAXSIM's otherprop column is
non-QBI by definition and grants zero - and (b) the hand-computed statutory
QDCGT worksheet (Rev. Proc. 2025-32 brackets and capital-gains thresholds,
validated against TAXSIM's own v19 ordinary-tax column, 147/147 joint and
60/63 single exact) reproduces axiom's tax_before_credits to the dollar
FROM AXIOM'S OWN TAXABLE INCOME. The tax_before_credits residual is
therefore exactly the taxable-income convention gap times the marginal
rate: -400.00 x 0.37 = -148.00 on the top-bracket rows (the -148 cluster),
-639.13 x 0.22 = -140.61 and -721.49 x 0.22 = -158.73 on the 22%-bracket
rows. Same bridge convention, not a rules disagreement; resolves with the
parent entry when the projection surface gains a QBI-capable column.

Triangulated to TAXSIM's capital-gains bracket vintage by hand-computing
the statutory QDCGT worksheet from TAXSIM's OWN taxable income (v18) with
Rev. Proc. 2025-32 parameters, brackets first validated against TAXSIM's
own v19 ordinary-tax column (147/147 joint, 60/63 single exact). The
worksheet exceeds TAXSIM's v28 by a flat 134.79 on joint rows and 67.40 on
single rows across all income levels: TAXSIM's 2026-05-21 module projects
the 0% capital-gains threshold forward from the 2025 value (96,700 MFJ) at
its own inflation assumption (implied threshold 99,798.61) instead of the
published 98,900, sheltering 898.61 more gain at 0% - 898.61 x 0.15 =
134.79, halved for single filers (449.31 x 0.15 = 67.40). Rows between 2
and the fingerprint straddle the threshold partially. Axiom matches the
published Rev. Proc. values; a TAXSIM-side parameter vintage, resolved
when NBER re-bases the 2026 thresholds.

Composite/de-duplication face of the unit's own component classes, the
same contract as liability-composite-of-member-classes-and-niit-addmed-scope:
on every selected row the federal liability residual reproduces within the
concept's $15 tolerance (178 of 181 within $1) as

  d(tax_before_credits) + d(amt) - d(ctc) - d(eitc) - d(cdcc) - niit

where the component deltas are this same report's own rows and niit is the
pinned binary's idtl=2 niit column (the documented §1411 carve-out,
axiom-encode#1213). fiitax carries NO addmed term - verified against the
pinned binary: fiitax equals v28 + v27 - v22 - v25 + niit exactly on these
rows (e.g. 73,767.02 + 159.83 = 73,926.85 on ecps-tax-unit-135629). The
liability face therefore adds no information beyond the component rows; its
mismatch mass is already counted once at the concept where each mechanism
originates (QBID rental-convention bridge shadow, TAXSIM capital-gains
threshold vintage, CTC/EITC 2026 machinery gaps, AMT class, NIIT scope),
and those root-cause rows retain their own dispositions or remain openly
unexplained rather than being laundered through this composite.

Triangulated TAXSIM-side divergence in Colorado's credit stack, the same
mechanism and proof standard as taxsim-co-refundable-credit-vintage in
co-state-income-tax-taxsim: on every selected row axiom and PolicyEngine
agree on Colorado liability (the tax unit is absent from the complete
31-row axiom-vs-PE mismatch set of
dashboard/public/data/axiom-policyengine-co-state-income-tax-ecps.json over
the same 1,201-unit population), while TAXSIM departs. The pinned binary's
idtl=2 decomposition locates the divergence in TAXSIM's state credit
columns (sctc family-affordability/CTC and sptcr; e.g. sctc 2,528.67 on
ecps-tax-unit-58696) plus a before-credits component on units whose federal
taxable income carries the dispositioned QBID rental-convention gap
(Colorado starts from federal taxable income, so -400.00 x 0.044 = -17.60
flows through). Deltas are heterogeneous because the credit stack varies
per household; the per-row proof is the axiom==PolicyEngine agreement. The
seven units where that triangulation FAILS (the documented
co-state-open-rows-axiom-pe-divergent class) are excluded and stay raw.

Formerly the open-investigation rows blocked on triangulation; both
blockers are now closed. (1) The axiom-vs-PolicyEngine divergence on all
seven units is dispositioned bridge_artifact per row in
axiom-policyengine-co-state-income-tax-ecps (the PE-leg input-projection
differences), so the axiom Colorado value stands as the attributed
reference. (2) A fresh idtl=2 rerun of the pinned binary now reproduces
ALL SEVEN TAXSIM values to the cent from freshly projected input rows -
including 135552, which previously failed from the persisted row - and
each decomposes exactly as siitax = staxbc - sctc - sptcr - 0.5 x v25:
135552: 0 - 2,528.67 - 41.20 = -2,569.87; 135799: 974.42 - 1,657.50 -
20.60 = -703.68; 135880: -20.60 - 0.5 x 351.40 = -196.30; 136208:
10,317.46 - 37.82 = 10,279.64; 136404: 237.16 - 2,134.82 - 20.60 =
-1,918.26; 58696: -2,528.67 - 41.20 - 0.5 x 664 = -2,901.87; 59285:
18,429.21 - 63.86 = 18,365.35. The members are the catalogued
TAXSIM-side ingredients: the Colorado EITC coupling of the 2026
childless-schedule federal EITC (dispositioned
taxsim-2026-eitc-childless-schedule-applied; 58696: 0.5 x 664 = 332 vs
axiom 0.5 x 6,997.18), the CO child-credit and family-affordability
vintage (dispositioned taxsim-co-refundable-credit-vintage), the
mstat=1-with-dependents auto-HoH standard deduction (136208), and
TAXSIM's automatic itemization of its own computed state income tax
(59285). Axiom's Colorado value is the attributed reference here
because the PE divergence is dispositioned, not because it was
independently hand-verified against statute on these units.

Triangulated to TAXSIM's AMT parameter vintage by hand-computing Form 6251
from the published parameters: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 exemptions (90,100
unmarried / 140,200 joint), the H.R.1 section 70107 phaseout (50% rate from
500,000 / 1,000,000), the 244,500 28%-rate threshold, and the section
55(b)(3) Part III worksheet at the regular 0/15/20 breakpoints. On every
selected row axiom's AMT reproduces that statutory computation within $5 —
two independent implementations (the composed bridge worksheet and the
verifier's model, built separately from the same published parameters)
agreeing — while TAXSIM's v27 departs (it matches the same statutory model
on only 3 of 39 rows; its 2026-05-21 module carries pre-OBBBA
exemption-phaseout geometry, consistent with the capital-gains threshold
vintage dispositioned as taxsim-2026-capgains-zero-threshold-vintage).
Deltas are heterogeneous because the exemption phaseout interacts per
household; the per-row proof is the axiom==statute agreement. Rows where
axiom itself is not yet on statute stay raw.

Triangulated TAXSIM-side QBID machinery gap. On every selected row
TAXSIM's own identity v18 = v10 - v13 - qbid holds within $1, so the entire
taxable-income residual is the QBID difference — the two AGIs agree. The
implied axiom deduction (taxsim qbid minus the residual) lands exactly on
the H.R.1 section 70105 $400 minimum deduction or on zero. These units sit
far above the section 199A(b)(3) phase-in ceiling, where the deduction is
limited to 50% of W-2 wages / UBIA; the activity carries no W-2 wages, so
the statutory regular deduction is extinguished and only the $400 floor
survives — which is what axiom grants. TAXSIM's qbid column shows roughly
20% of (psemp minus half SE tax): its 2026-05-21 module applies the 20%
rate without the wage/UBIA limitation (and, on rows where its qbid is
below 400, without the section 70105 minimum). Axiom matches statute;
TAXSIM's QBID machinery vintage does not.

Extension of taxsim-2026-capgains-zero-threshold-vintage to the full
capital-gains bracket set. Modeling TAXSIM with BOTH 2026 thresholds
projected from the 2025 values at its own ~3.204% inflation assumption
(0% rate: 96,700 -> 99,798.61 joint / 48,350 -> 49,899.31 single; 15% rate:
600,050 -> 619,283 joint / 533,400 -> 550,494 single) reproduces its v28
within $1.50 on every selected row, while the same worksheet at the
published Rev. Proc. 2025-32 values reproduces axiom's tax_before_credits
from axiom's own taxable income within $5. The compound fingerprints
confirm it in closed form: rows straddling both thresholds show exactly the
sum of the two effects (134.79 + 280.53 = 415.32 joint; 67.40 + 249.29 =
316.69 single, where 280.53 = (619,283 - 613,700) x 0.05 and 249.29 =
(550,494 - 545,500) x 0.05 within rounding of the projection factor).
A TAXSIM-side parameter vintage across its 2026 capital-gains bracket set;
axiom matches the published values. Resolves when NBER re-bases.

Dual parameter-vintage defect on the section 461(l) excess-business-loss
limitation, fully characterized and favoring neither engine. On every
selected row the taxable-income residual reproduces to the dollar as the
unit's aggregate business loss (negative SE income net of positive rental)
minus a 461(l)-shaped cap that the axiom leg applies and TAXSIM does not:

  ecps-tax-unit-155431: 32,912,356.00 - 610,000 = 32,302,356.00
  ecps-tax-unit-156922:  1,010,637.94 - 610,000 =    400,637.94
  ecps-tax-unit-154480: (710,192.62 - 13,201 rental) - 305,000 = 391,991.67

Neither side matches 2026 statute: TAXSIM deducts the FULL loss (its module
carries no 461(l) limitation at all), while the caps the axiom leg applies
- 305,000 single / 610,000 joint - are the 2024 inflation-adjusted values,
not 2026's (no 461 encoding exists in the pinned rulespec-us checkout to
carry the current amounts; the cap arrives through the projection surface).
The residual is therefore a fully named two-sided vintage artifact: it
resolves when TAXSIM adds the limitation and the axiom-side cap is sourced
from a 2026-vintage 461(l) encoding. Until then the arithmetic above is the
complete accounting of each row.

Full-evidence member decomposition: on every selected row the
taxable-income residual equals, to the cent, the sum of exactly two named
